lintRules.name: scorp/no-raw-color
lintRules.description: No hex, rgb() or hsl() colors in component code. Use token-backed classes or var(--token).

lintRules.name: scorp/no-raw-scale
lintRules.description: Use semantic aliases (primary-*, secondary-*) rather than raw color scales, so the system stays re-themeable.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-rounded
lintRules.description: Scorp DS is sharp-cornered. Use rounded-none, or the plate-round silhouettes.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-arbitrary-values
lintRules.description: No bare numeric literals in Tailwind arbitrary values. Route through a token, or allowlist with a reason.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-undefined-css-var
lintRules.description: Every var(--name) must be a custom property that exists: declared in tokens.css (or one of the app stylesheets), or declared by the same file. Decision 0023.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-default-tailwind
lintRules.description: The preset extends Tailwind rather than replacing it, so Tailwind's own palette, shadows, radii, durations and fonts still compile. None of them are tokens.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-slow-motion
lintRules.description: Interactive states animate in at most --duration-normal (200ms). --duration-slow and --duration-slower are for overlays entering or leaving, in allowlisted files. Decision 0025.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-style-literals
lintRules.description: No raw sizes, colours, durations or fonts in inline style objects. Class rules cannot see style={{}}; values there go through var(--token) too.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-deep-import
lintRules.description: Import other packages through their public barrel, never from their src/ internals.

lintRules.name: scorp/prop-jsdoc
lintRules.description: Every member of an exported *Props interface or type has a JSDoc comment. JSDoc on the prop is what autodocs, the IDE and api-surface.json read; @param on the function reaches none of them.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-off-scale-spacing
lintRules.description: Padding, margin, gap and space utilities use a step from global.spacing (whole or half). Tailwind's own extra steps (7, 9, 11, 14, 28, …) are not tokens. Decision 0027.

lintRules.name: scorp/no-legacy-package
lintRules.description: The old @sachahurley/scorpion-ui package must never be imported.

lintRules.name: scorp/story-skip-visual-reason
lintRules.description: A `skip-visual` tag removes a story from visual regression, so it must say why in a comment (decision 0012). Usually a timer or randomness.

lintRules.name: scorp/story-interaction-needs-play
lintRules.description: A story named for a state no prop can set (focus, hover, press, drag) must drive itself there with a play function, or visual regression captures the resting state (decision 0012).

lintRules.name: scorp/no-element-focus-in-story
lintRules.description: Story play functions must drive focus with the keyboard. :focus-visible does not match programmatic focus, so element.focus() renders no ring while still looking like passing coverage.

lintRules.name: scorp/public-jsdoc
lintRules.description: Every exported component needs a JSDoc comment explaining usage.

workflows.name: CI
workflows.summary: Fast correctness gate: lint, types and unit tests on every PR.
workflows.note: Kept separate from storybook-a11y.yml so it fails in ~1 minute instead of waiting on a full static Storybook build.
steps: Specs match the components they describe
Token tables in design-tokens.md are current

workflows.name: Deploy Storybook
workflows.summary: Deploys the built Storybook to GitHub Pages on every push to main.
workflows.note: https://sachahurley.github.io/scorp-ds/ This is the public reference-docs URL that consumer sites (the lean showcase, the portfolio) link out to instead of duplicating docs.

workflows.name: main health
workflows.summary: Keeps one GitHub issue honest about the state of main: opened (or commented
workflows.note: on) when a check on main fails, closed when everything is green again. You only hear about main when it is broken. See docs/decisions/0019. Report only: this workflow never pushes, never edits code, and needs no secrets beyond the default token. Two ways in: - Whenever CI, Storybook a11y or Deploy Storybook finishes on main. - Weekly, and by hand: the full ds-health.sh plus an npm audit report, which catch what a push cannot (a dependency advisory published since the last merge). The audit is reported in the run summary and does not open the issue until decision 0018's gate is in place.
steps: Open, update or close the issue

workflows.name: Storybook a11y
workflows.summary: Builds static Storybook, serves it locally, runs @storybook/test-runner + axe on all non-skipped stories.
steps: Glyph audit (no character may fall back to a system font)

workflows.name: Visual regression
workflows.summary: Screenshots every story in both themes and diffs against committed baselines.
workflows.note: Baselines are platform-specific: font rasterisation differs between macOS and Linux, so a baseline captured on a laptop will never match here. They are generated and compared ONLY in this container. Two ways to refresh them (decision 0020): - Put [update-baselines] in the message of a pull request's latest commit. This job then rewrites the frames that changed, commits them to the branch, and re-runs the required checks on that commit. Review the PNGs in the pull request's "Files changed" tab; GitHub shows before and after. - Run this workflow by hand with `update` (and `force` for a Chromium or runner upgrade). That uploads the baselines as an artifact to commit by hand, which is the only route for a branch with no pull request.

1-bit pixel-art icon set

decisions.title: Consumers vendor a committed copy
Semantic aliases only, never raw scales
Both token files are hand-maintained
Specs live in the repo only
Every "never" gets a check that fails
One rule weight in the system
One size scale: sm | md | lg
Stories drive their own interactions via play
--update writes only the baselines that changed
Case studies are structured pages, not block lists
CI checks are required to merge into main
Spec drift fails CI
Every component has a story and a test, held by a ratchet
Pin actions to commits; Dependabot moves them
The health of main is one GitHub issue
Visual baselines are refreshed by a commit tag
Consumers are built against a change before it merges
Text-field focus is a colour change, not an inset ring
Semantic tokens are referenced by variable; every variable is checked
One prop vocabulary, and one way to deprecate a name
The 200ms cap is for interactive states; overlays may take longer
A spec is stable when it meets a checkable bar
Half-step spacing gets tokens; off-scale steps are errors
Composition rules are written down, and every pattern is a preset
An interactive component's accessible name is required by its type

insights.title: Strong components, but the step from component to screen still needs a human
The checks were good; nothing made them block
Baseline byte churn is anti-aliasing, and the fix is in what --update writes
The hardcoding rules cost almost nothing to enforce, because the code already complied
Most agent tooling described a stack this repo does not use
